Hi, and welcome back to the show. Before we start, a few of you wrote in and asked who I actually am, so here it is, in one minute. My name is Nicole and I live in Portland, Oregon. I work from home four days a week. I walk my two dogs every morning before I do anything else, and most evenings I wind down with a book, not with a party. I am a homebody. People find that strange, because this is a travel show, but it is true. The difference is that twice a year I close the laptop and I go somewhere far. Last spring my husband and I rented an RV and we drove up through Alaska for two weeks. We did not stay in a single hotel. We cooked in the RV, we woke up next to a river, and every mile of it was worth it. So that is me. A homebody who travels.

Hi there, you have reached the front desk at Riverbend RV Park, just outside Denali. Nobody is at the desk right now, so here is what you need to know. Check-in is any time after two in the afternoon. Your site number is on the board by the gate, and the key to the restrooms is in the little envelope with your name on it. Quiet hours start at ten. If this is your first time here, one piece of advice: fill your water tank tonight, not tomorrow morning, because the line gets long. The store closes at eight, so grab whatever you need before that. And one more thing. The sky stays light until almost midnight this time of year, so do not trust the sun to tell you when to sleep. Enjoy the park, and we will see you in the morning.

Here is the thing nobody tells you in a classroom. The English in your book is real English. It is simply not the English that anybody says out loud. In the book you read, what are you going to do this evening. On the street you hear, whatcha gonna do tonight. Those are the same words. Nothing was taken away. They were only pushed together, because we speak in beats, not in letters. That is why a student who understands every word on the page can stand in a store in Anchorage and catch nothing at all. It is not a vocabulary problem. It is a rhythm problem, and rhythm is learned by ear, never by rule. So here is my advice for this week. Take one minute of any American show, play it four times, and say it along with the speaker until your mouth moves at their speed. One minute, four times. That is the whole method.
